findings.fix: Drop `NAMESPACE` and the `strip_comments_and_strings` call, and collect names via `for _, kind, name in scopes(raw): if kind == "namespace" and name:`. `scopes` additionally requires the namespace command to be the whole line; if that restriction actually changes the collected name set, keep the regex but say so in a comment rather than leaving an unexplained parallel parser.
findings.issue: `NAMESPACE` and its use in `mathlib_namespaces` (lines 151-153) re-implement namespace-command parsing that the module extracted by this PR already provides: `lean_source.scopes` (lean_source.py:259-272) matches the same modifier prefix (`public|private|protected|noncomputable`), the same `[\w'.]+` name class, and already strips comments/strings internally.

findings.fix: Export the shared pieces from `lean_source` — e.g. `namespace_components(stack: list[Scope]) -> list[str]` and `qualify(name: str, stack: list[Scope]) -> str` — define `qualified_declarations` on top of them, and use them at lint-dot-notation.py:308-314 and :342 instead of the inline comprehension and `_root_.` test.
findings.issue: `find_violations` re-derives the namespace flattening and `_root_.` rooting that `qualified_declarations` performs at lean_source.py:440-444 (`[component for scope in stack for component in scope.components]`, `_root_.` check, `".".join`). The de-duplication PR therefore leaves the qualification rule implemented twice, in two files, where they can drift.

`skip_balanced` is imported but never used; it is a leftover of the extraction (the only remaining balanced-delimiter scans in this file are the inline loops in `_top_level_notation_receiver` and `_binder_has_type`).

summary: The move itself is clean and no other script duplicates the parser, but the consumer keeps a second namespace-matching regex and a second copy of the scope-flattening/_root_ rooting logic that the newly extracted module now provides, plus one dead import.
